messages.subject: Air quality mapping routes
messages.body:
Hi Paul,

I'm a UofT student on co-op in London, UK, working on search, planning and simulation for biotech automation, mostly around failure and recovery in large systems. I've also done a fair bit with RL and MCTS.

The planning work has made me interested in problems where the decisions you make also determine what you get to observe. Aclima’s mobile mapping seems like an interesting case, since the route determines what you learn about how pollution varies across an area and there’s only so much ground you can cover.

I was wondering if there might be a small contract project I could take ownership of alongside my current work. One idea would be to compare driving plans in simulation and look at what each one misses under the same time constraint, though I’d much rather work on whatever problem would actually be useful to the research team.

My resume is attached for context; happy to talk if there’s something worth exploring.

Best,
Andrew

messages.subject: Recovering delivery plans after delays
messages.body:
Hi Scott,

I'm a UofT student on co-op in London, UK, working on search, planning and simulation for biotech automation, mostly around failure and recovery in large systems. I've also done a fair bit with RL and MCTS.

A lot of the planning work I’m doing now is about what to do once the original plan stops being valid, and I’d like to do more of that outside biotech. Routific seemed interesting for that reason. If one delivery runs late, there’s a tradeoff between replanning enough to recover the schedule and changing so much that you create new problems elsewhere.

I was wondering if there might be a small contract project on that kind of recovery problem that I could take ownership of alongside my current work. One possible starting point would be to simulate delays and compare different replanning strategies by how much lateness they recover and how much of the original route they disrupt. But I’d rather work from a problem the team already cares about than force that exact idea.

I attached my resume for context. Happy to talk if there’s something worth exploring.

Best,
Andrew
